To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the global dynamics of the reaction-diffusion system with memory is governed by a family of regular exponentially attracting sets which are robust with respect to e → 0.
a singularly perturbed reaction-diffusion problem with memory is well-posed and generates a dynamical semigroup which is dissipative and asymptotically smooth.

, for e small enough, the Cauchy- Dirichlet problem for the reaction-diffusion with memory generates a semigroup which is dissipative and possesses a regular global attractors of finite fractal dimensions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the asymptotic behavior of solutions to a singularly perturbed hyperbolic equation, which is a model of a reaction-diffusionequation with memory.
the study of the asymptotic behavior of a reaction-diffusive system with a memory kernel κ, when κ is small.
the asymptotic behavior of a reaction-diffusionequation with memory in the singular limit of vanishing memory kernel.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the reaction-diffusion system with memory is asymptotically stable and possesses a regular exponential attractor of finite Hausdorff dimension, provided that the memory kernel κ is summable and sufficiently small.
the reaction-diffusion system with memory is well-posed, and its solutions exhibit regular dissipative dynamics.
the reaction-diffusion system with memory exhibits a regular global attractors with finite fractal dimension, provided that the relaxation time is sufficiently small.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have proved that the reaction-diffusion problem with memory has a global attractor which is regular and has finite fractal dimension and which attracts all the trajectories of the Cauchy- Dirichlet problem with a rate independent of the relaxation time e.
the reaction-diffusion system is asymptotically approximated by an ordinary differential equation in a suitable topology.
, in a two-dimensional setting, the reaction-diffusion problem with memory has a regular global attractors of finite dimension.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in order to obtain the existence of a finite-dimensional global attractor for a reaction-diffusionequation, it suffices that the memory kernel κ is sufficiently "close", in a certain sense, to the Dirac mass.
the presence of a memory kernel can be regarded as a small perturbation of a hyperbolic equation with nonlinear damping.

the memory term can be treated as a perturbation of the diffusion term in the standard reaction-difference equation, and that this perturbation does not affect the qualitative behavior of the solutions, as long as the memory is "small" (in the above sense).
